key_insight: Fréchet Distance — long seen as impractical to optimize directly — can be efficiently minimized in a learned representation space by decoupling the large sample population used for FD estimation from the smaller batch used for gradient updates (FD-loss). This enables direct training toward distributional/perceptual metrics.
problem_solved: Makes Fréchet-based objectives practical for training visual generative models by resolving the computational/sample-size mismatch that previously prevented stable gradient optimization of FD.
method: Compute Fréchet Distance in a chosen representation space (e.g., pretrained encoder features) rather than pixel space to capture perceptual statistics.
Decouple the FD estimation population size (large, e.g., 50k) from the gradient batch size (smaller, e.g., 1k) so estimates remain stable while gradients are efficient.
Use the resulting FD-loss to post-train or fine-tune a base generator, improving alignment with distributional/perceptual metrics.
impact: Provides a practical recipe (FD-loss) to optimize generators directly for distributional/perceptual quality, enabling better visual fidelity and metric alignment without prohibitive computation. This is immediately useful for model fine-tuning and evaluation-driven training.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram: data flow showing large population for FD estimation vs small batches for gradient updates (two parallel pipelines converging to FD-loss).
Embedding illustration: images mapped to representation space with Gaussian fitting and Fréchet distance computation between real and generated feature distributions.
Before/after image grid: visual comparison of generator outputs pre- and post-FD-loss fine-tuning.
Line chart: FD (or perceptual metric) vs training steps showing faster/stabler decline when using FD-loss compared to baselines.
paper_title: Representation Fréchet Loss for Visual Generation
paper_authors: Jiawei Yang, Zhengyang Geng, Xuan Ju, Yonglong Tian, Yue Wang
